messages.subject: Dynocc multi-season model error bar problem
parts:
Hey everyone!

I am applying multi-season dynamic occupancy models to large mammal species in Turkey by using single-species camera trapping data.

I have a problem by having full error bars (from 0 to 1) for some species depending on various variables and I couldn't figure it out the problem. Since my detection history (presences) are relatively sparse, I decided to build models with 2 different environmental variables at a time for one population parameter. I selected the final model by trying out all of the variables and based on their AIC comparisons.

For example for S.scrofa species, the final model is selected as:

library(unmarked)

sscrofa <-unmarkedMultFrame(y = data1,
                            siteCovs = data.frame(habitat=habitat, province=province, town=town, 
                                                  elevation=elevation, slope=slope, aspect=aspect),
                            yearlySiteCovs = list(season=season),numPrimary = 6)




dm_sscrofa <- colext(psiformula = ~ province,
                     gammaformula = ~ season + elevation + season:elevation,
                     epsilonformula = ~ season + province + season:province,
                     pformula = ~ slope,
                     data = sscrofa)


and when I try to get the results for colonization (gamma -  whis is affected by season, elevation and their interaction) with predict function the outcome is:

nd_col <- expand.grid(season=c('S', 'W'), elevation = seq(-2.489484, 1.321115, length.out = 6))  # this is the new data set for predict function, S for summer and W for winter

dat_col = cbind(nd_col,predict(dm_sscrofa, type='col', newdata=nd_col)) # this is the final result with covariates and predicted means, used for plot



ggplot(dat_col,aes(elevation,Predicted,col=season,group=season))+
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5))+
  ylab('Colonization')


Why do I get this full error bars when I predict results from the model? 
Additionally, if the effect of elevation is this bad to the gamma, why is this model selected among others as the best parsimonious model?

Any help would be appreciated.

Thank you,
Dilsad

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Dynocc multi-season model error bar problem
parts:
Dear Dilsad,

looking at the estimates, I note that both point estimates and SEs are extremely large (in absolute terms). This suggests that something has gone wrong in the estimation. From your umf summary one can see that your data set does not seem to be too sparse, but nevertheless, I think that your model may be too complex for it. Try a step-up model buildin strategy, starting with the simplest model (with 4 intercepts) and then adding covariates one by one. Not as a formal strategy of model selection, but just to be better able to diagnose the source for numerical problems in fitting the model. As soon as you get such extremely large point estimates and/or SEs, you know that the term added last causes this problem.

Indeed, AIC can select a model with useless estimates, for instance, in the context of the binomial N-mixture model, AIC often tells you that a model with Negative binomial abundance mixture fits best, by far, and yet it predicts totally unrealistically high levels of abundance. To be honest, I don't fully understand this (OK, it may be due to boundary estimates, see also Dennis et al., Biometrics, 2015 and Kery, Ecology, 2018). But perhaps one thing to learn from this is: the best-fitting model is not necessarily the model that you should use. But I digress....

So, try that step-up modeling strategy. And remember that you don't need to try out all possible covariate combinations in your model, or even many variables, to be a good scientist. Some respectable people say that you can just build a single model, which makes sense to you based on what you know about the system, on your available data and your questions. See this paper: https://wildlife.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jwmg.891

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Dynocc multi-season model error bar problem
parts:
Dear Dilsad,

yes, I do think that your model is probably too complex for the data set. Or you could have problems with complete separation, in which case ML estimation in binary regression-types of models (such as the dynocc) breaks down.

At any rate, the CIs are a function of your SEs (which are on the logit scale). And all of your SEs, except those for detection, are between 100 and 1000. You can to plogis(-100) and plogis(100) in R and you get 0 and 1.

Best regards  ---- Marc
